cell.justification: The vendor's own support page states a dated end of support for the Team plan, 31 March 2030, more than 12 months out, which meets the level-5 condition.

selectors.exact: The Team plan is supported until 31 March 2030.

missing.note: Retrieval covered the Larkpad website, the Larkpad changelog and two independent review sites and returned no span on a support window.

selectors.exact: Business plan customers are supported through December 2029.
Mossnote Business: end of support announced for June 2026.

missing.note: Retrieval covered the Mossnote pricing page and a reseller catalogue. The vendor page states support through December 2029 (level-5 condition); the reseller entry states end of support in June 2026 (level-1 condition). Nothing dates or supersedes either, so nothing chooses between them.

cell.justification: The help centre states every workspace exports to Markdown and JSON with a published JSON schema, which meets the level-5 condition; the API reference qualifies this with an open schema for bulk-endpoint exports and contradicts nothing. Reading 'every workspace' as 'all data' is an inference, hence medium.

selectors.exact: Export every workspace to Markdown and JSON; the JSON schema is published in our API reference.
Exports produced by the bulk endpoint are documented in the open Notes Interchange schema, version 2.

missing.note: No retrieval record for this cell and no spans were handed in, so it has not been searched yet.

cell.justification: The help centre states notes and folders export to plain Markdown but comments and attachments export only as a proprietary bundle, so the evidence is past the level-3 condition (proprietary only) and short of the level-5 condition (all data open): a level between anchors 3 and 5.

selectors.exact: Notes and folders export to plain Markdown. Comments and attachments export only as a .mossarchive bundle, readable by Mossnote.

cell.justification: The help centre says the team can move off Quillbase self-serve at any time, with completeness limited by the export formats its data supports; that is the level-3 condition (self-serve path with stated limits), not level 5.

selectors.exact: You can move your team off Quillbase yourself at any time. How complete the move is depends on the export formats your data supports; see the export guide.
Industry-leading support, there for your team whenever you need it.

missing.note: Retrieval covered the Larkpad homepage and press releases. The only span returned is a generic homepage line about support staff, which makes no commitment on how long support lasts for any plan, so no span places this cell.

cell.justification: The vendor's own help centre states migration is handled by its paid Migration Services team, and a consultancy blog says a paid engagement is required above 50 seats; both meet the level-1 condition and nothing conflicts.

selectors.exact: Moving an organisation off Mossnote is handled by our paid Migration Services team.
Mossnote requires a paid engagement with its own services team to migrate an organisation of more than 50 seats.

cell.justification: The vendor's help centre describes a self-serve migration assistant with a stated limit, since it carries across only what the export tool can produce; that is the level-3 condition, not level 5.

selectors.exact: Larkpad's migration assistant moves your workspace without any help from us, and it carries across exactly what the export tool can produce, nothing more.

cell.justification: The developer docs state every workspace, including comments and attachments, exports as JSON under a published schema, meeting the level-5 condition; the schema being open is read from its being published.

selectors.exact: Every workspace, including comments and attachments, exports as JSON that follows the published OpenNotes 1.2 schema.
